note: Rewritten from Sands 1972, original in English (The soldierless termites of Africa (Isoptera: Termitidae), Bulletin of the British Museum (Natural History), Entomology, the relevant volume of Supplement 4; this is the entry for Adaiphrotermes choanensis (Fuller) comb. n., synonym Mirotermes (Procubitermes) choanensis Fuller, 1925: 184). The original description was based on Fuller's 1925 specimens from Pretoria, South Africa, and this entry also designates the lectotype: Transvaal, Pretoria, Arcadia, 1914-11-23, collected by C. Fuller, type nest, deposited in the National Collection of Isoptera, Pretoria; the paralectotypes are from the same nest, some in the AMNH. Sands records 39 nest series and notes that Fuller had placed a soldier of the genus Lepidotermes together with alates of the same batch, and that another tube contained an alate of Astalotermes; these specimens have been separated from the lectotype and paralectotypes. The second half of the measurement table (the remaining entries for the left and right mandible) has values and row names misaligned in the OCR and is not recorded. The original uses a small comma and an asterisk for the decimal point and multiplication sign (e.g. 0*872); here they are rendered as a decimal point. Figs 634—637 (alate head capsule in front and lateral view, mandibles) are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The typical form of the alate is larger, darker and has a distinctly raised fontanelle, which clearly separates it from Adaiphrotermes cuniculator and A. scapheutes; smaller, paler individuals with a flat or sunken fontanelle appear under unfavourable conditions and may recur after several years, so that the species has been mistakenly divided into two. In the worker the fore tibia is slightly less swollen than in the other species, but the gut characters appear more specialized.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule from sepia-brown to dark sepia-brown, jet black above the ocelli; the fontanelle ranges from very small, circular, slightly depressed and concolorous with the head to larger than the ocelli, white, raised and elongate-oval; the central spot is circular to oval, about a quarter the size of an ocellus, usually slightly raised; the postclypeus is sepia-brown, the labrum yellowish brown; the frontal maculation is variable, usually distinct, crescent-shaped, bare and flat; the antennae are pale brown. The pronotum is sepia-brown, the mesonotum and metanotum brown without dark sutures; the femora and tibiae of the legs are brown and the tarsi pale yellow. The abdominal tergites are sepia-brown with the dorsal spiracles pale brown; the sternites are brown, paler at the midline, and the ventral spiracles also brown; the cerci are yellowish white. The posterior margin of the head capsule is evenly rounded; the ocelli are medium-sized, at one half to two thirds of their minimum diameter from the compound eye; the postclypeus is medium-sized to large and moderately swollen, postclypeus length/head width 0.20—0.30, its posterior margin evenly rounded and its median suture distinct. The pilosity of the head capsule is slightly uneven, with many long hairs not yet matted into felt, brown. Measurements (23 individuals, 14 localities, mm, mean ± standard deviation in parentheses): head width (with compound eyes) 0.71—0.96 (0.872 ± 0.063); ocellus 0.06—0.09 × 0.08—0.12 (0.072 ± 0.007 × 0.095 ± 0.010); ocellus to compound eye 0.03—0.06 (0.044 ± 0.009); postclypeus length 0.18—0.25 (0.222 ± 0.021); antennal segment 3 0.01—0.03 (0.015 ± 0.004); segment 4 0.03—0.05 (0.032 ± 0.006); segment 5 0.02—0.04 (0.030 ± 0.006); left mandible, apical tooth to first marginal tooth 0.05—0.08 (0.067 ± 0.009); left mandible, first to third marginal tooth 0.09—0.15 (0.131 ± 0.016); left mandible, third marginal tooth to molar area 0.05—0.07 (0.061 ± 0.006); right mandible, apical tooth to first marginal tooth 0.05—0.08 (0.069 ± 0.009).
